questions.prompt: Do people in your country like planting vegetables?

answers.basic: Some people do, even if they only have a balcony. Back in Hunan, growing a few spring onions or chillies at home felt quite normal. A relative of mine grows them in pots because she likes being able to cut a few fresh ones when she's cooking.

questions.prompt: Were there any kind of fruits and vegetables you disliked as a child?

answers.basic: I didn't like bitter melon when I was little. I remember taking one bite and then trying to eat the rest of my rice around it. The bitter taste was much stronger than I expected, and even mixing it with other food didn't help much.

questions.prompt: What kind of fruits and vegetables do you dislike?

answers.basic: Bitter melon still isn't my favourite because the taste stays in my mouth for a long time. I'm happy with most other vegetables. I quite like vegetables with a little heat, though, so I'd happily have something like peppers with my dinner.

questions.prompt: Where do you usually buy fruit and vegetables?

answers.basic: I usually pick them up at a supermarket near home. If I get back late from coaching, I sometimes order a few things to be delivered. I like being able to choose the fruit myself when I have time, especially if I'm buying enough for several days.

questions.prompt: How often do you eat fruit and vegetables?

answers.basic: I try to have vegetables with lunch or dinner every day. Fruit is usually a snack, especially if I'm hungry between work and badminton. A banana is easy to carry in my bag, so I sometimes eat one on the way to a lesson.
